First, I need to break down each component. Request routing involves how requests are directed to different parts of the cluster. Maybe using a queuing system like a priority queue or a round-robin. Queueing would be about how data is stored and processed. Tail latency is the time a request spends waiting for the tail to process, which could be affected by the queue length and processing speed.

Cache transfer is about how data moves between the cache and main memory. Latency here would be the time taken for data to move, which could be minimized by efficient cache management. Role switching refers to when a request changes the processing role, like from a CPU to a GPU, which affects GPU utilization and throughput.

Batch completion is the time taken for a batch of requests to finish. GPU utilization here would be the percentage of GPU time used, which is crucial for throughput. Throughput tradeoffs involve balancing between processing speed and resource usage, like how much GPU time is allocated versus CPU time.
